commands.title: Connect to MySQL
commands.description: Opens an interactive MySQL client on the local server and asks for the password.

commands.title: Connect to a remote MySQL server
commands.description: Connects to a server on another host and port; the account must be allowed to log in from your IP.

commands.title: Connect to one database directly
commands.description: Opens the client with the given database already selected.

commands.title: Run one query and exit
commands.description: Runs a single statement and prints the result; replace the statement with your own.

commands.title: Show all databases
commands.description: Lists the databases the account can see.

commands.title: Show tables in a database
commands.description: Lists every table of the given database.

commands.title: Describe a table
commands.description: Shows the columns, types and keys of a table.

commands.title: Dump one database to a file
commands.description: Consistent dump of an InnoDB database without locking tables, including stored routines; asks for the password.

commands.title: Dump all databases
commands.description: Dumps every database including routines and events into one file; asks for the password.

commands.title: Dump a single table
commands.description: Exports only one table of a database.

commands.title: Dump a database and gzip it on the fly
commands.description: Pipes the dump straight into gzip so the uncompressed file never touches the disk.

commands.title: Restore a database from a .sql file
commands.description: Imports a dump into an existing database; existing tables of the same name are overwritten if the dump drops them.

commands.title: Restore a database from a .sql.gz file
commands.description: Decompresses the dump on the fly and feeds it to mysql; the database must already exist.

commands.title: Create a database with utf8mb4
commands.command: mysql -u <user> -p -e "CREATE DATABASE <database> CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci;"
commands.description: Creates a database that fully supports Unicode including emoji.

commands.title: Create a user and grant access to a database
commands.command: mysql -u <user> -p -e "CREATE USER '<newuser>'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED BY '<password>'; GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON <database>.* TO '<newuser>'@'localhost'; FLUSH PRIVILEGES;"
commands.description: Creates a local account with full rights on one database; the password ends up in your shell history.

commands.title: Show grants for a user
commands.description: Lists the privileges granted to the account.

commands.title: Change a user password
commands.description: Sets a new password for the account; the password ends up in your shell history.

commands.title: Flush privileges
commands.description: Reloads the grant tables after editing them directly; not needed after GRANT or CREATE USER.

commands.title: Show running queries
commands.description: Lists every connection with its current query, state and run time.

commands.title: Kill a running query
commands.description: Stops the statement of the given process id but keeps the connection; get the id from SHOW PROCESSLIST.

commands.title: Show database sizes
commands.command: mysql -u <user> -p -e "SELECT table_schema AS db, ROUND(SUM(data_length + index_length) / 1024 / 1024, 1) AS size_mb FROM information_schema.tables GROUP BY table_schema ORDER BY size_mb DESC;"
commands.description: Reports the data plus index size of every database in megabytes.

commands.title: Show table sizes in a database
commands.command: mysql -u <user> -p -e "SELECT table_name, ROUND((data_length + index_length) / 1024 / 1024, 1) AS size_mb FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema = '<database>' ORDER BY size_mb DESC;"
commands.description: Lists the largest tables of one database first.

commands.title: Check and repair all databases
commands.description: Checks every table and repairs the ones that are corrupted; mostly useful for MyISAM.

commands.title: Optimize all tables in a database
commands.description: Defragments tables and refreshes statistics; can lock tables while it runs.

commands.title: Check slow query log status
commands.command: mysql -u <user> -p -e "SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'slow_query%'; SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'long_query_time';"
commands.description: Shows whether the slow query log is on, where the file is and the time threshold.

commands.title: Show MySQL service status
commands.description: Shows whether the server is running; on MariaDB or RHEL-style systems use mariadb or mysqld instead.

commands.title: Restart the MySQL service
commands.description: Restarts the server and drops every open connection; on MariaDB use mariadb.

commands.title: Run the secure installation script
commands.description: Walks through setting the root password, removing anonymous users and the test database.

commands.title: Connect to PostgreSQL
commands.description: Opens psql against the given host and database; asks for the password.

commands.title: Open psql as the postgres superuser
commands.description: Uses peer authentication of the local postgres system account, no password needed.

commands.title: Connect with a connection URI
commands.description: Connects using a URI; add ?sslmode=require for remote servers that need TLS.

commands.title: Run one SQL command and exit
commands.description: Runs a single statement and prints the result.

commands.title: List databases
commands.description: Shows all databases with owner, encoding and access privileges.

commands.title: List tables in a database
commands.description: Lists the tables of the public schema; use \dt *.* for every schema.

commands.title: Describe a table
commands.description: Shows the columns, indexes and constraints of a table.

commands.title: Dump a database in custom format
commands.description: Compressed archive that pg_restore can restore selectively and in parallel.

commands.title: Dump a database to a plain SQL file
commands.description: Plain text dump that can be restored with psql.

commands.title: Dump all databases and roles
commands.description: Dumps every database plus users and permissions into one SQL file.

commands.title: Restore a custom-format dump and replace objects
commands.description: Drops each existing object before recreating it, so current data is overwritten.

commands.title: Restore a plain SQL dump
commands.description: Runs the SQL file against an existing, usually empty, database.

commands.title: Create a database
commands.description: Creates a database owned by the given role.

commands.title: Drop a database
commands.description: Deletes the database and all of its data; fails while other sessions are connected.

commands.title: Create a role interactively
commands.description: Asks whether the role is a superuser and creates it with a password prompt.

commands.title: Change a user password
commands.command: sudo -u postgres psql -c "ALTER USER <user> WITH PASSWORD '<password>';"
commands.description: Sets a new password for the role; the password ends up in your shell history.

commands.title: Grant all privileges on a database
commands.command: sudo -u postgres psql -c "GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE <database> TO <user>;"
commands.description: Gives the role full rights on the database, but not on tables created by others in it.

commands.title: Show database sizes
commands.command: psql -U <user> -c "SELECT datname, pg_size_pretty(pg_database_size(datname)) AS size FROM pg_database ORDER BY pg_database_size(datname) DESC;"
commands.description: Lists every database with a human-readable size, largest first.

commands.title: Show table sizes
commands.command: psql -U <user> -d <database> -c "SELECT relname, pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size(relid)) AS total FROM pg_catalog.pg_statio_user_tables ORDER BY pg_total_relation_size(relid) DESC LIMIT 20;"
commands.description: The 20 largest tables including their indexes and TOAST data.

commands.title: Show active connections
commands.command: psql -U <user> -c "SELECT pid, usename, datname, state, query FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state <> 'idle';"
commands.description: Lists sessions that are currently running or waiting on something.

commands.title: Terminate a backend connection
commands.description: Forcibly closes the session with the given pid, rolling back its transaction.

commands.title: Vacuum and analyze a database
commands.description: Reclaims dead rows and refreshes planner statistics for the whole database.

commands.title: Reindex a database
commands.description: Rebuilds every index of the database; takes locks so run it off-peak.

commands.title: Show the config file location
commands.description: Prints the path to postgresql.conf of the running server.

commands.title: List PostgreSQL clusters
commands.description: Debian and Ubuntu helper that shows version, port, status and data directory of each cluster.

commands.title: Restart the PostgreSQL service
commands.description: Restarts all clusters and drops every open connection.

commands.title: Test the connection with ping
commands.description: Replies PONG when the local server is reachable.

commands.title: Connect to a remote Redis with a password
commands.description: Opens an interactive session; -a puts the password in the process list, prefer REDISCLI_AUTH.

commands.title: Show server information
commands.description: Prints version, clients, memory, persistence and stats sections.

commands.title: Show memory usage
commands.description: Shows used memory, peak, fragmentation ratio and the memory limit.

commands.title: Count keys in the current database
commands.description: Returns the number of keys in the selected database.

commands.title: Find keys by pattern with KEYS
commands.description: Blocks the server while scanning every key; avoid on production, use SCAN instead.

commands.title: Find keys by pattern with SCAN
commands.description: Iterates keys incrementally without blocking the server.

commands.title: Get the value of a key
commands.description: Prints a string value; use hgetall, lrange or smembers for other types.

commands.title: Set a key
commands.description: Creates or overwrites a string key.

commands.title: Delete a key
commands.description: Removes the key and returns how many keys were deleted.

commands.title: Show the time to live of a key
commands.description: Seconds left before expiry; -1 means no expiry, -2 means the key does not exist.

commands.title: Set a key expiry
commands.description: Makes the key expire after the given number of seconds.

commands.title: Watch every command in real time
commands.description: Streams every command the server receives; slows the server, stop it with Ctrl+C.

commands.title: Show the slow log
commands.description: Prints the 10 most recent commands that exceeded the slowlog threshold.

commands.title: Flush the current database
commands.description: Deletes every key in the selected database.

commands.title: Flush all databases
commands.description: Deletes every key in every database on the server.

commands.title: Show the maxmemory setting
commands.description: Prints the memory limit in bytes; 0 means unlimited.

commands.title: Find the biggest keys
commands.description: Samples the keyspace and reports the largest key of each type.

commands.title: List connected clients
commands.description: Shows address, age, idle time and last command of every connection.

commands.title: Connect with a connection URI
commands.description: Opens mongosh using a mongodb:// or mongodb+srv:// connection string.

commands.title: Connect to a local server with authentication
commands.description: Opens mongosh and asks for the password.

commands.title: Show databases
commands.description: Lists databases with their sizes without opening an interactive shell.

commands.title: List collections in a database
commands.description: Prints the collections of the database named in the URI.

commands.title: Dump a database with a URI
commands.description: Writes BSON dumps of every database the URI can read into a folder.

commands.title: Dump one database
commands.description: Compressed single-file archive of one database.

commands.title: Restore a dump and drop existing collections
commands.description: Drops each collection before restoring it, so current data is replaced.

commands.title: Restore a gzip archive
commands.description: Restores a database from an archive made with mongodump --archive --gzip.

commands.title: Export a collection to JSON
commands.description: Writes one JSON document per line.

commands.title: Export a collection to CSV
commands.description: CSV export needs an explicit comma-separated field list.

commands.title: Import a JSON file into a collection
commands.description: Inserts the documents from a file with one JSON document per line; add --jsonArray for arrays.

commands.title: Show database statistics
commands.description: Prints object counts, data size, storage size and index size.

commands.title: Count documents in a collection
commands.description: Returns the exact number of documents; pass a filter inside the braces.

commands.title: Create a user with a role
commands.command: mongosh "<uri>" --eval "db.createUser({ user: '<newuser>', pwd: '<password>', roles: [{ role: 'readWrite', db: '<database>' }] })"
commands.description: Creates a user in the current database; the password ends up in your shell history.

commands.title: Show current operations
commands.description: Lists operations currently running on the server.

commands.title: Show MongoDB service status
commands.description: Shows whether the mongod service is running.

commands.title: Open a database
commands.description: Opens the interactive shell and creates the file if it does not exist.

commands.title: List tables
commands.description: Prints the names of all tables.

commands.title: Show the schema
commands.description: Prints the CREATE statements of every table and index; add a table name for one table.

commands.title: Run a query from the shell
commands.description: Runs one statement and exits.

commands.title: Export a table to CSV
commands.description: Writes the query result with a header row as CSV.

commands.title: Dump the database to SQL
commands.description: Writes the schema and all data as SQL statements.

commands.title: Restore a database from a dump
commands.description: Rebuilds a database from a SQL dump into a new file.

commands.title: Check database integrity
commands.description: Prints ok when the file is not corrupted.

commands.title: Vacuum a database
commands.description: Rebuilds the file to reclaim free space; needs room for a temporary copy.
